status: F23-F26 confirmed and corrected; recorded Linux and browser checks passed

findings.correction: EPUB ZIP metadata and manifest declarations impose media-specific uncompressed budgets before extraction and cache publication. The reader checks declared limits before fetch and cancels streamed responses that exceed actual byte budgets. Text decoding is bounded before DOM construction.

CBZ and CBR preflight all entries, retained page count and retained size before staging. Only supported page images and one bounded ComicInfo.xml are persisted. Ignored entries are streamed through integrity validation into a discard sink. Free space is checked against retained bytes plus a reserve. Unsupported image formats remain explicit errors.

FB2-specific source and encoding limits are enforced before fingerprinting or buffering. Plain XML and file-backed ZIP entries feed an incremental decoder and bounded XML parser. One validated PreparedFb2 representation passes from inspection to preparation; production does not retain the wrapper or decompress and parse it again. UTF-16 decoding handles chunk boundaries and surrogate pairs.

Windows physical identity uses GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileIdInfo), retaining the entire 64-bit volume serial and 128-bit file identifier. Reparse and directory checks use FileAttributeTagInfo. Unsupported full-identity queries fail closed; legacy 64-bit journal identities cannot establish physical-instance proof.

additionalHardening: EPUB filename and declared media-type limits combine using the stricter budget; leading markup, BOMs and font signatures cannot evade textual or font limits by declaring a binary media type.
XML and HTML-like publication resources have bounded structural complexity before renderer parsing.
Warm-cache validation enforces resource budgets and rejects irrelevant retained comic resources before hashing.
RAR extraction bounds aggregate filename metadata, validates ignored CRCs, preserves cancellation and checks final output close errors.
FB2 limits include XML depth, node and attribute count, tag and text tokens, base64 images, prepared sections and aggregate prepared resources.

The review attachment paths were not mounted; supplied attachment bytes were not used. The EPUB has exactly 256 MiB of XHTML; each comic has one 75-byte PNG and two 64 MiB ignored binary entries.

limitations: No Windows compiler, Windows host or ReFS volume was available. Full 128-bit formatting and distinguishing high identifier/volume bits are covered by portable tests; the real Windows identity integration test is supplied and skipped on Linux.
Resource budgets deliberately reject publications that exceed the documented limits. Compressed archives still undergo bounded integrity work for ignored entries.
Pressure RSS is a preparation-process measurement, not a total-application memory claim.
